thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert P2 — spike in Sentry ingest errors and upstream 429s detected. Missing exception events coming from the mobile SDKs. Paging @lina (oncall).

lina (oncall): oncall here, reading the alert. seeing a spike starting ~08:12 UTC. linking logs and traces now. anyone else seeing this?

sam (sre): seeing it in the gateway too. Sentry backend getting a flood of 429/503 from our observability vendor (collector.prod). stacktraces are dropping on the ingestion path. initial hypothesis: vendor rate-limiting + token throttling after a key rollover.

josh (eng): can you paste an example of the upstream 429?

sam (sre): here's a snippet from the ingress proxy logs:

```
[2026-03-15T08:12:17Z] svc=sentry-ingest upstream=collector.prod status=429 x-request-id=abcd1234 body="rate_exceeded"
[2026-03-15T08:12:58Z] svc=sentry-ingest upstream=collector.prod status=503 x-request-id=efgh5678 body="temporarily_unavailable"
```

lina (oncall): confirmed. also seeing SDK-level errors in our mobile telemetry: `Failed to send events: 429 (rate_limited)` and `504`.

incidents-bot: Incident created: https://redwood-incidents/internal/1846000001 — severity=P2 — oncall=lina — triage-owner=sam

cara (cs): are there customers calling in? i got a ping from a customer complaining their error dashboard is empty since ~08:15. not many so far but flagged.

sam (sre): quick impact summary:
- Missing exception ingest for ~08:12-08:40 UTC window for events proxied through collector.prod.
- Affected SDKs: mobile (iOS >=1.8.0 older token refresh flow), some serverless lanes using buffered-mode.
- Customer-facing: few customers reporting missing events in dashboards; no data loss confirmed yet for persisted stored events, but realtime triage is delayed.

josh (eng): mitigation options:
1) Flip Sentry SDK to sync flush for mobile (force immediate send) — reduces batching but may spike requests.
2) Lower sampling rate at the SDK side to reduce load (e.g. sample_rate=0.1).
3) Enable local file buffering and retry outbound (SENTRY_OUTBOX_ENABLED=true) so events stay local until vendor recovers.
4) Route traffic to the vendor fallback endpoint or our internal fallback collector.

lina (oncall): can we do 2 and 3 quickly? sampling change is low risk. file buffer is supported by the Android/iOS SDKs via env toggle (we have a rollout plan).

josh (eng): i'll open a small config patch to lower sampling and enable outbox for mobile. will push canary to 10% of mobile traffic first.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: patch/sentry-mobile-fallback (canary=10%) by josh — queued, will execute in 2m.

sam (sre): also opening a request to vendor: https://status.collector.prod (ticket #INC-9982) — they replied: "Investigating increased error rates; customer tokens undergoing throttling due to recent key rotation. ETA unknown."

lina (oncall): has vendor given list of affected token prefixes or cred types? if it's the rotation, clients using older client-secret flow may be impacted.

sam (sre): vendor replied: "We are seeing high retry behavior from clients using implicit refresh; recommend rotating to new key material. We are temporarily rate-limiting per-credential to protect service."

cara (cs): copying support ticket template for customers: "We are aware of delayed/missing error events since 08:12 UTC due to a 3rd-party ingestion vendor rate-limiting. We're mitigating by reducing SDK sampling and enabling local buffering; we'll update when vendor recovers. If you rely on real-time triage, please DM us and we'll prioritize."

lina (oncall): current mitigations in progress:
- josh: canary config change to mobile SDKs (sample_rate=0.1 + SENTRY_OUTBOX_ENABLED=true) — deploy in progress.
- sam: contacted vendor and escalated to vendor on-call.
- I'll add temporary alert for high drop rate and create a saved query for missing exception signals.

josh (eng): canary is in. logs show initial flush requests still 429, but sample volume dropped ~85% and we see some successful deliveries to fallback.

deploy-bot: Deployment successful: patch/sentry-mobile-fallback — canary=10% applied.

lina (oncall): increasing canary to 50% now?

josh (eng): increasing to 50%.

deploy-bot: Deployment update: canary=50% — rolling.

sam (sre): good — monitoring shows error rate at ingestion falling from peak 18k/min to ~2k/min after sampling + outbox enabled. upstream 429s still present but less hit to our pipeline.

cara (cs): i've sent a customer update to the impacted customers list, included mitigation steps and a contact path. one customer asked for an estimated time to full recovery. i set expectation: "vendor is investigating; we anticipate gradual recovery as vendor lifts throttles and after client-side sampling takes effect; we will update within 2 hours."

lina (oncall): we should also enable a fallback forwarder to our internal S3 sink for events that fail to be sent to vendor — any objections?

josh (eng): low-risk: we can flip a runtime flag to forward failed payloads to s3 for later replay. I'll prepare a patch but it's not instant.

sam (sre): action list so far:
- josh: canary mobile config change (sample + outbox) — done (50%).
- josh: prepare s3-forwarder patch (in progress).
- sam: vendor escalation + monitor.
- lina: create incident ticket + schedule postmortem owner.
- cara: customer communications.

incidents-bot: Note: oncall handover flow — please confirm if @lina will hand off to second shift.

lina (oncall): i'll be handing off to @josh for the overnight watch at 12:00 UTC. summary pinned to incident.

josh (eng): i'll take the handoff. will keep monitoring for retries and forwarder progress.

sam (sre): follow-up: vendor posted status update at 08:35 UTC — partial mitigation in place; they will lift aggressive per-client throttles gradually. our ingest metrics show fewer 5xx/429s after 08:40. still patchy.

cara (cs): customers are asking if any events were permanently lost. do we have a clear answer?

sam (sre): short answer: we haven't found evidence of durable storage loss for events that reached our ingest — however, events that never left client due to client-side SDK failures may be lost unless outbox buffering is enabled. we will run a reconciliation job to compare SDK-side attempt counts vs server-side receipts.

lina (oncall): ok, for the postmortem please include: root cause (vendor rate-limit during key rotation), mitigation timeline (canary changes, outbox enable, s3 forwarder plan), customer impact list, and follow-ups (better vendor SLAs, automatic fallback to internal sink, SDK upgrade guidance).

josh (eng): quick commands used:
```
# flip sample rate and enable outbox for mobile deployment
kubectl set env deployment/mobile-sdk SAMPLE_RATE=0.1 SENTRY_OUTBOX_ENABLED=true -n prod
# verify rollout
kubectl rollout status deployment/mobile-sdk -n prod
```

lina (oncall): moving to monitoring-only mode. will hand off to josh at 12:00 UTC as planned.

josh (eng): got it. i'll track the ticket and own the overnight watch. assigning postmortem owner: sam.

incidents-bot: Incident 1846000001 updated: status=mitigated (reduced customer impact), owner=josh, postmortem_owner=sam

cara (cs): thanks team — i'll keep customers informed and consolidate incoming support cases for the PM/CS review. :thumbsup:

sam (sre): tagging for postmortem: action items include vendor SLA request, SDK auto-outbox default, integration tests for key rotation, and a durable replay pipeline for failed events.

lina (oncall): thanks everyone. :wave: I'll close the active paging for now and hand off to josh.

josh (eng): :eyes: will continue monitoring and post updates in the incident ticket.
